product_brief: Integrated device management, OTA update service, and certificate lifecycle management solution for IoT.
pqc_capability_description: PQC ready. Supports Pure PQC (ML-DSA) and Composite certificate issuance/renewal over EST, SCEP, ACME, CMPv2, and REST API. Includes batch issuance, client/server keypair generation, and automated lifecycle management for ML-DSA and composite certificates.
crypto_primitives: ML-DSA, ML-KEM, RSA, ECDSA, EdDSA, X25519, AES, SHA256
fips_validated: Not stated (Document mentions FIPS 140-3 certification for associated SDKs/HSMs, but does not explicitly state validation status for Device Trust Manager itself)
primary_platforms: IoT devices, Linux devices (via TrustEdge CLI), Embedded systems (via TrustCore SDK)
pqc_roadmap_details: Supports ML-DSA and ML-KEM. Industry transition aims for CNSA 2.0 compliance by 2027 and phase-out of old algorithms by 2030.
cryptographic_discovery_&_inventory: Supports utilization of Software Bill of Materials (SBOMs), Crypto Bill of Materials (CBOM), and Hardware Bill of Materials (HBOM) to identify crypto/TLS libraries and PQC readiness.
constrained_device_&_iot_suitability: Designed for IoT. Notes that new PQC x.509 certificates are roughly 10x larger, which can be problematic for constrained devices regarding memory and protocol handling.
supply_chain_&_vendor_risk: Supports SBOM/CBOM/HBOM generation. Relies on partners like Thales for HSMs and OQS for OpenSSL providers.
deployment_&_migration_complexity: Supports phased approach (Discover, Test, Deploy, Manage). Requires handling larger certificate sizes, multiple certificates for backward compatibility, and OTA updates for crypto libraries and root stores.
organizational_readiness: Requires cryptographic agility, engagement with standards bodies (NIST, IETF), and vendor roadmap alignment.

product_brief: Quantum-safe encryption for connected devices using post-quantum cryptography on ESP32 chips.
pqc_capability_description: Successfully delivered quantum-safe encryption for connected devices using post-quantum cryptography (PQC) on ESP32 chips. The encryption was tested using only PQC and combining PQC with traditional security, maintaining strong performance with low delay and minimal power impact.
target_industries: Defence, aged care, home security, healthcare, drone tech, surveillance, military
testing_&_validation_methods: Tested in two ways: one using only PQC and one combining PQC with traditional security.
constrained_device_&_iot_suitability: Suitable for small, low-power devices; billions of devices worldwide run on ESP32; low delay and minimal power impact.

product_brief: A post-quantum cryptographic platform offering asymmetric, symmetric, and random number generation for IoT and networks.
pqc_capability_description: Offers post-quantum cryptographic solutions via three functions: asymmetric encryption (MASQ™), symmetric encryption (QEEP™), and strong random numbers (SEQUR™). Designed for IoT devices and networks, integrating with STM32CubeMX.
crypto_primitives: MASQ™ (asymmetric), QEEP™ (symmetric), SEQUR™ (random numbers). Specific standard algorithms (e.g., Kyber, Dilithium) are not explicitly listed.
architecture_type: Platform integrated with STM32 microcontrollers via STM32CubeMX.
pqc_roadmap_details: Supports transition to NIST PQC standards; provides strategies to upgrade existing solutions to be quantum-secure.
qrng_&_entropy_sources: SEQUR™ provides strong random numbers ("Entropy"). Specific protocol or compliance details are not stated.
constrained_device_&_iot_suitability: Designed for IoT devices and resource-constrained devices; integrates with STM32CubeMX.
deployment_&_migration_complexity: Allows upgrading existing solutions without major investments in new technology or infrastructure.
financial_&_business_impact: No major investments in new technology or infrastructure required.

product_name: SEALSQ IneS Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) solution
product_brief: PKI solution for adding digital certificates to electric and gas metering devices during manufacturing.
pqc_capability_description: SEALSQ is pioneering next-generation quantum-resistant chips and PKI services. The company has a post-quantum roadmap to support the future post-quantum transition, embedding Post-Quantum Cryptography into semiconductor solutions to protect against quantum threats.
key_management_model: Offline, distributed, and as-a-Service models; decentralized certificate issuance and lifecycle management
architecture_type: Cloud-native service; offline and distributed models
primary_platforms: North American manufacturing facilities; electric and gas metering devices
pqc_roadmap_details: SEALSQ has a post-quantum roadmap and is developing Post-Quantum Semiconductors and PKI services to address security challenges posed by quantum computing.
constrained_device_&_iot_suitability: Designed for IoT devices and critical infrastructure; supports offline provisioning without constant connectivity.
deployment_&_migration_complexity: Supports offline, distributed, and as-a-Service models; scales horizontally with decentralized certificate issuance.
